headwords: con nhà tông không giống lông cũng giống cánh
con sâu làm rầu nồi canh
con trâu là đầu cơ nghiệp

flags.why: This way of referring to a woman can be derogatory, and informal alone does not warn the learner adequately.
This is an ordinary colloquial scolding expression, so rare misleadingly discourages recognition of an everyday use.
The expression disparages someone as benefiting from family connections and needs a derogatory warning ([usage discussion](https://vietcetera.com/amp/vn/chu-voi-nghia-con-ong-chau-cha)).
This term for a newborn has a literary or old-fashioned character rather than being an ordinary casual label ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/con-do-eJJEg4Vu7GY8E.html)).
In the comparison 'như thương con đỏ', con đỏ means a newborn child, not the common people.
flags.fix: Nhà vua lo cho con đỏ được sống yên ổn. = The king cares that his people can live in peace.

flags.why: The example explains what someone calls a bra instead of using coóc-xê to refer to one.
flags.fix: Bà lấy chiếc coóc-xê trong ngăn tủ ra. = Grandma took the bra out of the drawer.

flags.why: A cuốc chĩa is a small hoe with several pointed tines, not a combined hoe and pitchfork ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/cuoc-chia-exOplJOwN8PZW.html)).
flags.fix: Gloss: small forked hoe with several long, pointed tines; example translation: He uses a forked hoe to turn the soil for vegetables.

flags.why: A drop of cà cuống refers to the flavouring essence, whereas this sense identifies the insect.
flags.fix: Con cà cuống này được bắt ở ruộng lúa. = This giant water bug was caught in a rice field.

flags.why: Cà giựt is primarily Southern usage and needs a regional label ([Southern dialect discussion](https://www.namkyluctinh.org/tac-gia-tac-pham/a-b-c-d/cao-thoai-chau/phuong-ngu-nam-bo.html)).
